# Blockworks Python client

> Repository-maintained synchronous, read-only Python SDK for the Blockworks API.
> This index describes this client; it is not official Blockworks documentation.

## Start here

- [README](../README.md): Installation, credentials, quickstart, namespaces, responses, errors, and streaming exports.
- [Executable example](../examples/read_and_stream.py): Fetch asset price history and export CSV to an explicit destination.
- [Route inventory](coverage.csv): All 226 pinned GET routes mapped to SDK methods; inventory is not live-validation evidence.

## SDK essentials

Use `from blockworks_client import BlockworksClient` and a context manager.
`BlockworksClient()` reads `BLOCKWORKS_API_KEY` at construction. Supply it through the
environment, never on the command line. Never print credentials or injected environment values.

Namespaces: `tabular`, `timeseries`, `charts`, `unlocks`, `monitoring`, `watchlists`.
For coins, discover IDs with `client.tabular.list("assets", ...)`, then request
`client.timeseries.single("asset-price", "1d", asset_id, timeframe="7d")`.
Read `response.body["data"]["point_schema"]` to interpret compact point arrays;
do not assume a fixed OHLCV column order. Provider fields, nulls, and timestamps
are preserved. The client does not fill gaps or normalize market data.

Methods return `BlockworksResponse` with `body`, `status`, `headers`, and
`request_id`. Native filters use exact provider names; convenience arguments use
SDK names such as `page_size`. See README for method signatures and conventions.

Reads make one request unless explicitly using `iter_pages` or `iter_batches`.
Series batches are capped at ten. Pagination is bounded and does not promise a
snapshot of a changing dataset. Use `export_list`, `export_batch`, `export_single`,
or `export_to` for CSV/JSONL; decoded methods reject `acceptFormat`.

Four upstream mutation operations are deliberately excluded. There is no async
API, implicit cache, scheduler, canonical storage, or automatic time-window stitching.
Python 3.12 is supported. Do not infer SDK support from newer upstream docs.

## Maintenance and pinned contracts

- [Architecture](architecture.md): Ownership, source layout, spec update procedure, and shared transport boundaries.
- [Spec manifest](../specs/manifest.json): Pinned specification URLs, hashes, and retrieval date.
- [Schema overlays](../specs/overrides.json): Narrow reviewed corrections to upstream schemas.
- [Generated route metadata](../src/blockworks_client/_generated.py): Supported paths, query names, enums, and required parameters.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): Package changes.

## Official upstream documentation

Search the official docs for provider concepts, endpoints, and parameters. Search
the local SDK docs above for what this client supports.

- [Official documentation index (live)](https://docs.blockworks.com/llms.txt): Current upstream index.
- [Official full documentation](https://docs.blockworks.com/llms-full.txt): Combined upstream documentation; load selectively when needed.
- [Data API overview](https://docs.blockworks.com/getting-started/data-api): Upstream concepts and API guidance.


The official docs describe the provider API. Local README
and pinned route inventory describe this SDK's supported behavior. The official
docs also cover products outside this SDK (event feed, MCP server, Datashares,
webhooks, write operations). If they differ, report the discrepancy and verify it
before changing SDK limits or assumptions.
